knowledge:
- key_parameters: sort_peaks=TRUE ;; in getPeaks, sorts the input genomic ranges. ;; paired=TRUE ;; in getCounts, specifies that the input BAM files contain paired-end reads. ;; by_rg=TRUE ;; in getCounts, specifies whether to group and split counts by read group (RG) tags within a single BAM file. ;; min_depth=guidance ;; in filterSamples, sets the minimum library size threshold (estimated as 10% of median library size if omitted). ;; min_in_peaks=guidance ;; in filterSamples, sets the minimum proportion of fragments falling within peaks (estimated as 0.5 times the median proportion if omitted). ;; non_overlapping=TRUE ;; in filterPeaks and readNarrowpeaks, reduces overlapping peaks to a non-overlapping set by keeping the peak with the strongest signal. ;; species=guidance ;; in getJasparMotifs, specifies the target species (defaults to "Homo sapiens"). ;; out=guidance ;; in matchMotifs, controls the output format (e.g., "matches" for binary matrix, "scores" for match scores, or "positions" for genomic coordinates). ;; background_peaks=guidance ;; in computeDeviations, allows passing a pre-computed matrix of background peak indices to control the normalization step.
- alternatives: getJasparMotifs=A wrapper around getMatrixSet from the TFBSTools package, which can be used directly for more advanced JASPAR queries. ;; matchKmers=Can be used instead of matchMotifs if analyzing de novo or unbiased kmer accessibility variations rather than known transcription factor motifs.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have sparse chromatin accessibility data (such as single-cell ATAC-seq, single-cell DNase-seq, or low-input bulk ATAC-seq) and want to identify transcription factors, motifs, or kmers that drive variation in chromatin accessibility across cells or samples.
- pitfalls: MulticoreParam will not work on Windows systems; Windows users must register SnowParam(workers = 1, type = "SOCK") or SerialParam() instead. ;; Downstream functions will fail if any peaks have zero fragments across all samples; always run filterPeaks to ensure every peak has at least one fragment. ;; Overlapping peaks can introduce bias; ensure non_overlapping = TRUE is set during peak filtering or narrowpeak reading. ;; Single-cell datasets often contain low-quality cells or empty wells; failing to run filterSamples to remove low-depth or low-signal samples will degrade the quality of the deviation calculations.

workflows.name: chromvar_analysis_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform a complete chromatin accessibility variation analysis from peak and alignment files to identify motif-driven accessibility deviations across single cells or samples.
input: peaks.bed (genomic coordinates of open chromatin peaks)
genome_sequence (BSgenome package matching the alignment genome)
workflows.stages: 1. Read genomic peaks using getPeaks. ;; 2. Read fragment counts from BAM files using getCounts to create a SummarizedExperiment. ;; 3. Add GC content bias to peaks using addGCBias. ;; 4. Filter low-quality samples using filterSamples and filter/resolve overlapping peaks using filterPeaks. ;; 5. Retrieve motif position weight matrices using getJasparMotifs and match them to peaks using matchMotifs. ;; 6. (Optional) Compute background peaks using getBackgroundPeaks. ;; 7. Compute bias-corrected deviations and Z-scores using computeDeviations. ;; 8. Compute and plot annotation variability using computeVariability and plotVariability. ;; 9. Project and visualize deviations in 2D space using deviationsTsne and plotDeviationsTsne.
workflows.code:
library(chromVAR)
library(motifmatchr)
library(Matrix)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(BiocParallel)
set.seed(2017)

register(MulticoreParam(8))

peakfile <- system.file("extdata/test_bed.txt", package = "chromVAR")
peaks <- getPeaks(peakfile, sort_peaks = TRUE)

bamfile <- system.file("extdata/test_RG.bam", package = "chromVAR")
fragment_counts <- getCounts(bamfile, 
                             peaks, 
                             paired =  TRUE, 
                             by_rg = TRUE, 
                             format = "bam", 
                             colData = DataFrame(celltype = "GM"))

data(example_counts, package = "chromVAR")

library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19)
example_counts <- addGCBias(example_counts, 
                            genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19)

counts_filtered <- filterSamples(example_counts, min_depth = 1500, 
                                 min_in_peaks = 0.15, shiny = FALSE)

filtering_plot <- filterSamplesPlot(example_counts, min_depth = 1500, 
                                    min_in_peaks = 0.15, use_plotly = FALSE)

ix <- filterSamples(example_counts, ix_return = TRUE, shiny = FALSE)

counts_filtered <- filterPeaks(counts_filtered, non_overlapping = TRUE)

motifs <- getJasparMotifs()

library(motifmatchr)
motif_ix <- matchMotifs(motifs, counts_filtered, 
                        genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19)

kmer_ix <- matchKmers(6, counts_filtered, 
                      genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19)

dev <- computeDeviations(object = counts_filtered, annotations = motif_ix)

bg <- getBackgroundPeaks(object = counts_filtered)

dev <- computeDeviations(object = counts_filtered, annotations = motif_ix,
                         background_peaks = bg)

variability <- computeVariability(dev)

plotVariability(variability, use_plotly = FALSE) 

tsne_results <- deviationsTsne(dev, threshold = 1.5, perplexity = 10)

tsne_plots <- plotDeviationsTsne(dev, tsne_results, 
                                 annotation_name = "TEAD3", 
                                   sample_column = "Cell_Type", 
                                 shiny = FALSE)
tsne_plots[[1]]
tsne_plots[[2]]
